proof-narrative-lean-equiv.evidence: S↔L: the derivation (lean:182-192) is sound, but its coefficient `iteratedLR` is a stub that gives wrong values. `| ν, (_lam :: μs) => iteratedLR ν μs` (l.108) drops λ₁, so c^{(2)}_{(1),(1)} evaluates to iteratedLR (2) [(1)] = 0 instead of 1. `lrCoefficient` returns 0 in all nontrivial cases (l.97-100). The class hypothesis is therefore false for actual Hecke characters: for ν = (2), β = 1⊗1 it forces χ = 0 against the true 1. It is inhabited only by the trivial all-zero model (l.197-207). The .ts authorNote (ts:22) still says the Lean is a "`1 = 1` placeholder … deferred via `sorry`", which no longer matches. S↔P: the identity is the standard parabolic-restriction (LR) rule and the sketch is the right one. It rests wholly on prop:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition, which is conditional in its own Lean (lean:19-23), and it states no q-range, while the md is over arbitrary H_n(R,q). It holds for Specht characters by polynomiality, but the prf does not say so.
